items.title: Presentation by the Representatives of CLI on Agenda Item No. 3.1 of the 476th RC Meeting. The representative of Crop Life India & Crop Care Federation of India made a joint representation on the subject in reference to the RC decision taken in its 476th meeting vide agenda item no. 3.1 on the issue of changes/modifications in the present guidelines formed in 347th RC meeting and later on revised in 380th RC meeting for Export related. The representatives explained the earlier guidelines and benefits of those guidelines. They requested to allow unregistered molecules for import for export and registered molecules from registered source in general category.
items.decision: After detailed deliberations on the issue decided that unregistered molecules for import for export in general category is allowed to enhance the export opportunities and ease of doing business. However, keeping in view the registered molecule usage in India and its possibilities of pilferage into Indian market, RC reiterated its earlier decision on the registration of registered molecules from registered source with confirm order only. The approved guidelines for unregistered molecules for import for export from any source in general category are attached as Annexure-2.1.1. The validity of the certificate shall be one year from the date of issue of the CR or till the time the molecule is registered for use in the country, whichever is earlier. The RC further directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to add these guidelines in the existing guidelines approved by RC in its 380th meeting and make a consolidated guideline. The same shall be put-up on the website for information of the stake holders.

items.title: Gazette Notification No. S.O. 5234 E dared 22.09.2026 issued by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare regarding prohibition of Paraquat Dichloride-Reg.
items.decision: RC perused the above notification issued by the central government wherein the Insecticide Paraquat dichloride is Inter-alia completely prohibited for its manufacture, import, distribution, sale and use in the country being hazardous and involves grave risk to the Public at large. Further the CR issued under section 9 of the Insecticides Act, 1968 shall stand cancelled. RC observed that in compliance with the said notification a public notice dated 06.10.2026 has already been issued by the Sectt. of CIB&RC for information and compliance from the stake holders. RC also notes that Haryana Pesticides Manufacturers’ Association (HPMA) had filed a CWP No. 34272 of 2026 challenging the notification dated 22.09.2026 before the Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. RC also perused the order dated 14.10.2026 passed by the Hon’ble High Court where in the petitioner had undertaken that they will neither sale, purchase or manufacture nor import of paraquat dichloride from today onwards. It also directed the respondents that no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners. RC observed that this order is only qua the petitioner’s member companies. A List of the Same is a part of record. RC decided to comply with the same and inter-alia directs the Sectt. of CIB&RC not to call back the CR from the petitioners.

items.title: Submission of the Report of the Committee constituted in 476th Registration Committee meeting held on 10.09.2026 under Agenda Item No. 11.1, regarding correction of chemical composition in products containing Indoxacarb as one of the active ingredients.
items.decision: The Registration Committee considered the report of the Committee constituted vide Agenda Item No. 3.2 of the 469th Registration Committee meeting held on 10.02.2026 and subsequently reconstituted vide Agenda Item No. 11.1 of the 476th Registration Committee meeting held on 10.09.2026, under the Chairmanship of Dr. Poonam Jasrotia, ADG (PP), ICAR, Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. The Committee was constituted to examine the registered formulations containing Indoxacarb, the inclusion of isomer ratio in their chemical composition, and the incorporation of isomer ratio requirements in product specifications to establish the distinctiveness of the technical material used in the manufacture of formulations. The Registration Committee appreciated the efforts made by the committee in collecting and analysing all the related information on the issue. The RC noted the findings of the report regarding the registration status of different technical grades of Indoxacarb and their associated stereo isomer ration in Chemical composition. The report indicated that Indoxacarb Technical 67% minimum, registered for indigenous manufacture, specifies a minimum of 50% active S-isomer and a maximum of 17% inactive R-isomer, whereas Indoxacarb Technical 90% minimum, registered under the import category, specifies a minimum of 90% active S-isomer and a maximum of 1% inactive R-isomer. The Committee further noted that the chemical composition, product specifications and Methods of Analysis of the registered Indoxacarb- based formulations do not uniformly provide for the separate determination of both isomers and their ratio. The Registration Committee also took note of the observations recorded in the report concerning the analysis of a referee sample of Indoxacarb 14.5% + Acetamiprid 7.7% SC, wherein the Central Insecticides Laboratory (CIL) observed an isomer profile containing only the active isomer of Indoxacarb. The report further recorded that the technical material corresponding to Indoxacarb Technical 90% minimum was not registered for domestic use under Section 9(4) of the Insecticides Act, 1968. In this context, the Committee noted the importance of establishing the stereoisomeric profile of Indoxacarb in formulations to facilitate verification of the approved technical source and detection of any possible use of unauthorized, unregistered or export-only technical material in formulations intended for domestic use. The report recommended that the chemical composition of all Indoxacarb- based formulations should clearly specify the total Indoxacarb content, active S-isomer content and inactive R-isomer content. It further recommended that the product specifications and Methods of Analysis should incorporate separate limits for total Indoxacarb, active S-isomer and inactive R-isomer, along with the acceptable S & R isomer ratio, as applicable. The report also proposed corrections to the declared Indoxacarb content and product nomenclature of certain registered formulations, as detailed in the report, wherever required, to account for the respective active and inactive isomer contents. As per available records, total Certificate of Registration holders of the indoxacarb as a sole A.I. or as one of the A.I. in combination is shown as Annexure-3.3.1. After detailed deliberations, the Registration Committee agreed with the recommendations of the Committee as contained in the report. The Registration Committee appreciated and commended the Chairman and all members of the Committee for their comprehensive examination of the registration records, scientific assessment of the isomeric composition of Indoxacarb technical grades and formulations, and formulation of recommendations aimed at strengthening product quality assurance, technical-source traceability and regulatory compliance. The Registration Committee agreed with the recommendations of the report regarding the incorporation of total Indoxacarb content, active S- isomer content, inactive R-isomer content and the acceptable S & R isomer ratio, as applicable, in the chemical composition, product specifications and Methods of Analysis of Indoxacarb-based formulations. The proposed corrections to the chemical composition and product nomenclature of the formulations identified in the report were also noted as part of the Committee's recommendations. The Registration Committee decided that the aforesaid decision shall be applicable prospectively as well as retrospectively. Accordingly, the requirements shall apply to all new applications received for registration of Indoxacarb-based formulations, applications presently under scrutiny at various stages of the registration process, and formulations already registered under section 9(3) & 9(4) of the Insecticides Act, 1968. The concerned applicants and existing registrants shall be required to comply with the prescribed requirements regarding chemical composition, product specifications and Methods of Analysis, including stereoisomer profiling, in accordance with the directions and regulatory procedure prescribed by CIB&RC. The Registration Committee further decided that CIB&RC shall issue a public notice for all concerned applicants and registrants of Indoxacarb-based formulations, communicating the formulation-wise corrected chemical composition and the applicable requirements for product specifications and Methods of Analysis, based on the recommendations accepted by the Registration Committee. Revised and approved Chemical identity of Indoxacarb to be replaced in all the CRs & Chemical Compositions by RC of all the registered formulations registered for use in the country and its revised Product Specifications with Method of Analysis are attached as Annexure 3.3.2. The notice shall clearly specify the requirements applicable to applications under scrutiny and formulations already registered, along with the necessary actions and timelines for compliance, as prescribed by CIB&RC. It was also decided there shall be no change in any other of the adjuvants or its quantity or purity what so ever may be. Only nomenclature of Indoxacarb is changed where Indoxacarb containing 75% S-active isomer and 25% in- active isomer has been approved by the RC in the approved formulation. The corrected formulation-wise chemical compositions shall be applicable to all the Certificate of Registration holders of the above said product. A general Public Notice cum endorsement letter shall be issued on the website for information and adoption by all the stake holders giving the revised Chemical composition of all registered formulation containing as one of the A.I. No separate endorsement shall be required for these purposes. The RC further directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC that the revised Chemical Composition (With isomeric ratio) along with Product Specification and Method of analysis shall be distributed to all the RPTLs/SPTLs and CIL for its use in quality control testing of the formulated product.

items.title: Verification of the CR issued to M/s Yashnee Agrochemicals India Private Limited purported for the product Aluminium Phosphide 56% Tablets & Registration no. CIR-17495/2023-APL (442).
items.decision: RC perused the agenda and observed that the applicant M/s Yashnee Agrochemicals India Private Limited had submitted a forged and fake CR to the Agricultural Pesticides Registration Authority at ECUADORS for the product Aluminium Phosphide 56% Tablets. RC also observed that the overseas regulatory authority had requested the Secretary CIB&RC for verification of the genuineness of the CR which as per records was not found to be genuine and issued by the RC. Accordingly, the same was communicated to the overseas regulatory authority. RC took a serious note of the same and apparently observed that the act committed by the applicant is unethical, illegal and amount to the commission of grave offence by tempering with the statutory document issued by the RC a regulatory authority under the Insecticides act, 1968. RC also feels it expedient that an opportunity to show cause is required to be given to the applicant to explain their conduct in the matter before taking any adverse view. RC directs the Sectt. of CIB&RC to issue a show cause notice to the applicant granting two weeks’ time to submit their reply. Thereafter, the matter may be placed before the RC by the concerned technical expert.

items.title: Follow up of agenda item no. 10.2 of 476 RC meeting held on 10.09.26 regarding application no. EN-48276 for endorsement of change of address of the source of Mis. Indofil Industries Ltd. under section 9(3) of the Insecticides Act 1968 approved by the RC in its 459th Meeting held on 03.10.2024 at Agenda item No. 9.105.
items.decision: RC perused the fact presented in terms of 476th RC decision and apparently observed that the applicant M/s Indofil Industries Ltd. despite the rejection of their chemistry endorsement application on merits by the RC in its 454th meeting itemized at agenda item no 10.18 had again applied for the same captioned chemistry endorsement vide a fresh application on the very same basis. Since, RC was unaware of the earlier rejection and therefore the same was approved by the RC in its 459th meeting and the certificate to this effect had also been issued by the CIB&RC through CROP Portal. RC after deliberations observes that such act of the applicant is purely unethical, and unwarranted especially in view of the fact that the applicant has neither filed an appeal against the rejection order passed by the RC nor the applicant had represented before the RC to review its decision rejecting the application of the applicant. RC apparently is of the view that once an application is rejected, no fresh application lies, thereafter on identical/similar grounds. RC is of the prima-facie view that such act of M/s Indofil Industries Ltd. and prima-facie tantamount to concealment of facts and is akin to play deception upon the Registration Committee, a statutory body constituted under the Insecticides Act, 1968. However, RC is of the considered view that before taking any coercive action against M/s Indofil Industries Ltd., an opportunity is required to be given to them to explain their stand in the matter explaining their conduct. RC also directs the Secretariate of CIB&RC to call the applicant for making a presentation in the next RC meeting so as to take a final decision in the matter. RC also directs the applicant to submit the presentation document well in advance before the secretariat of CIB&RC.

items.title: Follow up action of vide agenda item no. 10.55 of 476th RC meeting.
items.decision: RC deliberated the progress regarding E-KYC Compliance by the registrants and observed that a number of communications/public notices have already been issued by the Secretariat of CIBRC for E-KYC compliance by all stakeholders along with communication dated 09.03.2026 issued to the State/UT governments followed up by emails dated 25.04.2026, 10.06.2026, 17.08.2026 and 14.10.2026 along with list of such companies state and UT-wise for sensitizing the pesticide registrants/license holders for completion of KYC on CROP portal. However, around 900 no. of applicants have still not completed the KYC requirement on CROP portal due to which the said accounts are lying under frozen category. Hence, it was decided that a D.O. letter may be sent through the higher authorities in DA&FW to the Principal Secretaries of the respective state/UT governments for expediting completion of KYC by the remaining applicants in their respective states and UTs, if applicant is existing/interested.

items.title: Reconsideration of the requirement of Health Monitoring Studies for label expansion of Thiamethoxam 12.6% + Lambda-cyhalothrin 9.5% ZC of M/s Syngenta India Ltd. for control of household insect pests.
items.decision: RC recalled its decision under Agenda Item No. 10.34 of the 472nd RC Meeting regarding the requirement of Health Monitoring Studies for label expansion of pesticide formulations for household insect pest control. After deliberation, the RC decided to consider and approve the case, subject to the following conditions: 1. The applicant shall submit an affidavit stating that “The handling and use of this product shall be promoted as per the instructions depicted on the approved label and leaflet.” 2. The applicant shall submit revised labels and leaflets incorporating a cautionary statement that the product shall be used “only by certified and trained Pest Control Operators (PCOs)” and only in the recommended places/spaces, strictly in accordance with the approved label and leaflet. 3. The product shall not be used in hospitals, schools, Anganwadi centers, childcare facilities, food preparation and food storage areas, or other designated sensitive areas.

items.title: Issuance of a Public Notice for Disposal/Closure of Long-Pending Endorsement Applications and Other Pending Applications. With the permission of the Chair an agenda was presented containing a list of very old applications, some of them were transferred from NIC software system.
items.decision: The Registration Committee considered the proposal regarding the disposal/closure of long-pending endorsement applications and other pending applications before CIB&RC. The Committee deliberated on the need to streamline the processing of such applications and ensure their timely disposal. The Committee was of the view that a Public Notice may be issued by the Secretariat of CIB&RC advising the concerned applicants, registrants and other stakeholders to review the status of their pending applications as detailed in Annexure-11.1.1, and submit the requisite clarifications, information, documents or compliance, wherever required, within a stipulated period of 30 days from the date of issuance of the Public Notice. It may further be notified in the Public Notice that applications in respect of which no response is received from the concerned applicants within the stipulated period of 30 days shall be considered as closed. The Secretariat of CIB&RC shall accordingly take necessary action for issuance of the Public Notice containing the list of long-pending endorsement applications and other pending applications and subsequent disposal/closure of such applications.
